description: Finds events in a specified Google Calendar using text, time ranges, and event types. Results are returned in event_data.event_data and may span multiple pages; follow nextPageToken even when a page is empty.

calendar_id.description: Identifier of the Google Calendar to query. IMPORTANT: This must be a valid calendar identifier, NOT a calendar name/title. Valid formats are: 'primary' (the authenticated user's primary calendar), an email address (e.g., 'user@example.com'), or a calendar ID (e.g., 'abc123xyz@group.calendar.google.com'). To find the calendar ID for a named calendar, first use the List Calendars action (googlecalendar.list_calendars) to retrieve all available calendars with their IDs. 'primary' searches only the authenticated user's primary calendar; to search all calendars, retrieve each ID via googlecalendar.list_calendars and query separately.
calendar_id.human_parameter_description: Which calendar you want to search. MUST be 'primary', an email address, or a calendar ID - NOT a calendar name. To get the ID for a named calendar, first use List Calendars to find the ID.
calendar_id.title: Calendar Id

event_types.description: Event types to include. Supported values: 'birthday', 'default', 'focusTime', 'outOfOffice', 'workingLocation'.
event_types.human_parameter_description: Choose which kinds of events to include (like default events, birthdays, out of office). Leave as-is to include all types.

items.description:
Event type constraints:
- 'birthday': Requires transparency='transparent', description must be omitted
- 'outOfOffice': Requires calendar_id='primary', Workspace/enterprise calendar,
  transparency='opaque', location and attendees must be omitted,
  create_meeting_room must be false
- 'focusTime': Requires Google Workspace Enterprise account with Focus Time feature enabled
- 'workingLocation': Requires Google Workspace Enterprise account
items.title: EventType

event_types.title: Event Types

max_results.description: Maximum number of events per page (1-2500).
max_results.human_parameter_description: How many events to return per page of results. Larger numbers show more at once; smaller numbers are easier to scan.
max_results.title: Max Results

order_by.description: Order of events: 'startTime' (ascending by start time) or 'updated' (ascending by last modification time). Note: 'startTime' requires single_events=true. Use 'updated' if you need to include recurring masters (e.g., cancelled series).
order_by.human_parameter_description: How to sort the results—by start time or by last updated time. Pick start time for a chronological list.
order_by.title: Order By

page_token.description: Token from a previous response's `nextPageToken` to fetch the subsequent page of results. Always follow every `nextPageToken` until absent; skipping pagination silently omits events on busy calendars.
page_token.human_parameter_description: If you’re fetching the next page of results, paste the token from the previous response here.
page_token.title: Page Token

query.description: Free-text search terms to find events. This query is matched against various event fields including summary, description, location, attendees' details (displayName, email), and organizer's details. Cannot search by event_id. Performs full-text match (not exact); broad terms may return unrelated events. For person-based matching, prefer attendees[].email over display names. If results appear incomplete, use googlecalendar.events_list with client-side filtering.
query.human_parameter_description: The words or phrases to look for in events. Use this to find meetings by title, description, location, or people.
query.title: Query

show_deleted.description: Include events whose status is 'cancelled'. This surfaces cancelled/deleted events, not a separate 'trash' view. Behavior with recurring events: when single_events=true, only individual cancelled instances are returned (the recurring master is omitted); to include cancelled recurring masters, set single_events=false. If updated_min is provided, events deleted since that time are included regardless of this flag.
show_deleted.human_parameter_description: Whether to include events that were cancelled or deleted. Turn this on if you need to see removed events.
show_deleted.title: Show Deleted

single_events.description: When true, recurring event series are expanded into their individual instances. When false, only the recurring master events are returned. Note: Ordering by 'startTime' requires singleEvents=true. For large calendars, it is strongly recommended to specify both timeMin and timeMax to limit the expansion window and improve performance.
single_events.human_parameter_description: Whether to expand recurring series into individual events. Turn off to see just the main series entry.
single_events.title: Single Events

time_max.description:
Upper bound (exclusive) for an event's start time to filter by. Only events starting before this time are included. Accepts multiple formats:
1. RFC3339 timestamp (e.g., '2024-12-06T13:00:00Z')
2. Comma-separated date/time parts (e.g., '2024,12,06,13,00,00')
3. Simple datetime string (e.g., '2024-12-06 13:00:00') Set to the first instant after the desired period to avoid missing boundary events, especially all-day events (date-only fields). Overly wide ranges expand many recurring instances, causing large payloads and high latency — constrain to the minimum required window.
time_max.human_parameter_description: The latest date and time to include in your search window. Events starting after this won't be shown.
time_max.title: Time Max

time_min.description:
Lower bound (exclusive) for an event's end time to filter by. Only events ending after this time are included. Accepts multiple formats:
1. RFC3339 timestamp (e.g., '2024-12-06T13:00:00Z')
2. Comma-separated date/time parts (e.g., '2024,12,06,13,00,00')
3. Simple datetime string (e.g., '2024-12-06 13:00:00') RFC3339 timestamps must include explicit timezone offsets; missing or mismatched offsets can silently exclude matching events. To align with the calendar's timezone, retrieve it via googlecalendar.get_calendar.
time_min.human_parameter_description: The earliest date and time to include in your search window. Events before this won't be shown.
time_min.title: Time Min

updated_min.description:
Lower bound (exclusive) for an event's last modification time to filter by. Only events updated after this time are included. When specified, events deleted since this time are also included, regardless of the `show_deleted` parameter. Accepts multiple formats:
1. RFC3339 timestamp (e.g., '2024-12-06T13:00:00Z')
2. Comma-separated date/time parts (e.g., '2024,12,06,13,00,00')
3. Simple datetime string (e.g., '2024-12-06 13:00:00')
updated_min.human_parameter_description: Only show events that were changed after this date and time. Useful for finding recent updates.
updated_min.title: Updated Min
